references.text: Jacob called the place Bethel, but the city was originally named Luz. This refers to Jacob's earlier visit and naming of the place.
Abraham built an altar for the Lord at Bethel. This highlights the site's significance for the patriarchs.
Abraham returned to Bethel, the place where he had first set up an altar. This underscores Bethel's importance as a holy site.
Confirmation of the place's name and meaning: Bethel as 'House of God,' given after God's revelation.
Retrospective confirmation: Jacob identifies Luz as the place of God's revelation and blessing.
Historical confirmation: Confirms that Bethel was formerly called Luz, as described in the Genesis account.
Historical continuity: Confirms that the site was known as Bethel in later Israelite times.
